**Bottom line:** The market is arguing about whether the AI trade has broken, with a Fed hike on top. Wednesday's reversal and tonight's futures jump are being read as a bounce "still searching for a reason." Friday's half session is the test. These figures come from secondary summaries (CNBC, ZeroHedge, Investing.com). Their numbers differ slightly from yours, and I flag the conflicts below.

**1. AI and Nvidia: credibility and financing**
- Jensen Huang left Nvidia and was then reinstated. NVDA jumped 31% on Monday 11-23, when the S&P and Nasdaq had their best days since April 2025. NVDA has since fallen in 9 of 10 sessions, including -3.9% Wednesday to about 149.
- S&P put Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch negative over governance. Moody's held stable.
- Nvidia reportedly paused server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as US export controls tighten. Goldman calls it a pause, not a cancellation.
- Lenders reportedly paused data-center loans tied to ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent.
- The credit market isn't buying the bounce: Oracle CDS is at a record and CoreWeave at a new wide.
- The broader worry is debt-funded AI capex, signs of slowing spending, and rising rates.
- The Nasdaq-100 fell 4.7% intraday Wednesday, about 20% below its 10-6 record, then closed -0.6%. The SOX semiconductor index was down nearly 8% intraday and closed -0.65%.
- Goldman called the reversal "an abatement of supply," not a wave of buying. Panmure Liberum calls the dip buying a mystery.
- Offsetting this, China's October electronics profits doubled year to date on AI memory demand.

**2. The Fed is expected to hike, and the debate is how far**
- Odds of a hike on 12-9 are about 96-98%, under Chair Warsh. The fed funds range is 3.75-4.00%.
- Core PCE came in at 3.3% against 3.2% expected. Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% from 3.4%, and Trump called for an investigation of the revision. Jobless claims were 189k.
- Banks (JPM, BofA, Deutsche) expect further 25 bp hikes in January and March. Waller has kept a 50 bp hike on the table.
- Clients fear a replay of 2018, when the Fed hiked four times.
- The counter-argument is that the equity selloff itself could force a pivot. Citi and Bloomberg's Simon White make versions of it. Bill Ackman says the Fed is making a mistake.
- The 10-year yield is about 4.85-4.90%, off its highs.

**3. Oil and Middle East supply**
- WTI is about $84-86 and Brent about $92-95. The sources disagree on the exact levels.
- Houthi strikes hit Saudi ports (Jeddah, Jizan) and the Ras Tanura refinery. Iran claims tankers hit mines off Oman.
- Offsets: Hormuz tanker traffic rose this month, and OPEC+ may roll over its January quotas.
- Higher oil adds to inflation and hike risk, so it cuts against stocks.

**4. Tariffs**
- A Trump plan for higher tariffs on 14 trading partners (China, EU, Japan, India) is spooking markets. One item is a proposed 20% rate on China.

**5. Smaller stories**
- Japan Tobacco is reportedly exploring a takeover of Imperial Brands with Altria. Imperial rose 13% in London and said it received no offer.
- Gold is about $3,600-3,635, bitcoin is back above $60k, and the Bank of Korea hiked 25 bp.

**Numbers and conflicts**
- Futures at 9:18 PM ET (8:18 PM CT) were S&P +1.27% at 7,287 and Nasdaq-100 +1.8%. The Dow was +0.82%, and the US dollar index was 103.6. That matches your figures, but CNBC's earlier +0.7% and +0.6% were from the morning.
- Wednesday's S&P close was 7,183 (-0.25%) after falling as much as 3.2% intraday. VIX closed at 28.29 after peaking at 34.95.
- The week-to-date gain through Wednesday was S&P +3.9%, Nasdaq +4.3% and Russell 2000 +4.7%. November is still down about 3-7%, with the Nasdaq worst (-8.2%).
- Wednesday's Dow move is unclear: one source says +0.3%.

**What to watch:** Friday's thin half session, whether the rebound holds, Nvidia and AI credit spreads, further export-control news, oil and the Middle East, and the 12-9 Fed meeting.

agents.report:
**Story:** On Nov 25, after the close, Vertex (VRTX) said the FDA had pushed back its decision on povetacicept, its IgA nephropathy (IgAN) kidney drug. Shares fell about 7% after hours. The delay is not a rejection, but it removes the near-term approval catalyst the stock had run up into.

**What happened**
- The FDA told Vertex on Nov 24 that it was extending the review. The decision date moves from Nov 30 to no later than Feb 28, 2027. The cause was Vertex's response to a late-cycle FDA information request, which the FDA treated as a major amendment ([Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/vrtx-tumbles-hours-fda-delays-223419629.html), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/vertex-stock-rating-reiterated-by-jpmorgan-after-povetacicept-pdufa-delay-93CH-5052108)).
- Vertex said it "remains confident in the supporting data." It also warned that approval may not come by the new date, or at all.
- The stock had hit a 52-week high of $571.75 on Wednesday and closed flat near $564. It was up about 24% year to date ([Motley Fool](https://fool.com/investing/2026/11/25/vertex-could-land-its-fifth-franchise-on-nov-30-should-you-buy-before-the-fda-decides)). Our screen's 523.14 print was the reaction to the news, not a drift.
- Vera Therapeutics (VERA), which sells a rival IgAN drug (Trutakna), rose 17-18% after hours. The delay gives Vera more uncontested time on the market.

**Why the amendment is the open question**
- Vertex has not said what the information request covered. JPMorgan guessed it could be IgG monitoring or manufacturing.
- A Foley & Lardner citizen petition filed Oct 21 asks the FDA to require monthly IgG (immunoglobulin) blood tests and dose-hold rules in the label ([search summary](https://biotechcatalystcalendar.substack.com/p/ahead-of-vertexs-nov-30-fda-date), not opened directly). It cites five IgAN patients in the RUBY-3 study whose IgG fell below 300 mg/dL, all after Week 48.
- Vertex's position is that RAINIER, the Phase 3 trial behind the filing, had no opportunistic infections. Serious infections were 0.5% in both arms ([Life Science Daily](https://lifesciencedaily.news/povetacicept-fda-decision-rainier-30-november/)).
- A label with IgG monitoring requirements would weaken povetacicept against its rivals. The link between the delay and the petition is unconfirmed.

**Drug and competition**
- RAINIER's Week 36 interim analysis (199 patients) showed a 52% proteinuria reduction, and 42% of patients reached a proteinuria target (urine protein-to-creatinine ratio under 0.5 g/g) versus 6% on placebo. Safety looked clean ([Life Science Daily](https://lifesciencedaily.news/povetacicept-fda-decision-rainier-30-november/)).
- Otsuka's Voyxact (accelerated approval Nov 2025), Vera's Trutakna (July 2026) and Novartis's Fabhalta (full approval July 2026) are already on the market. Vera has filed for full approval and expects a decision in mid-2027.
- Povetacicept's eGFR (kidney function) data come later, in 2027. Approval would also be accelerated, based on proteinuria.

**Analysts and company backdrop**
- JPMorgan kept Overweight and a $570 target, with a 95% approval probability and $3.4B peak IgAN sales in 2035. It said PDUFA extensions tend to end in approval and called three months immaterial to peak potential.
- Other reported targets are Barclays $626, TD Cowen $575 and Stifel $563 (Hold). A search summary said Goldman and Barclays kept Buy ratings. I found no downgrades.
- Q3 revenue was $3.44B, up 12%. Guidance was raised to $13.15-13.25B ([SEC Q3 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/875320/000087532026000287/ex-991_q32026.htm)).
- Alyftrek (cystic fibrosis) had $706M in Q3 and Casgevy $99M. Journavx (pain) had $58M, and Palsonify (acromegaly drug from the Crinetics deal) $10M in its first month.
- Vertex closed the roughly $10B Crinetics acquisition on Sept 1. Non-GAAP EPS was flat year over year at $4.76, so the base cystic fibrosis business supports the stock but isn't the catalyst.

**What could move the stock over the next 1-10 sessions**
- **Friday Nov 27 half session (closes 12:00 PM CT):** The first regular-hours reaction to the news. Volume will be thin, and the gap could fade or extend. Vera's move is the cleaner read on the market's take.
- **Company or analyst follow-up:** Any detail on the amendment, or notes calling the delay benign. More reiterations are likely and are modestly supportive.
- **FDA action on the citizen petition:** A decision or hint on IgG monitoring is the biggest binary risk. It would more likely come near the Feb 28 deadline than in the next two weeks.
- **Unscheduled pipeline news:** The VX-670 interim data (DM1) are due in the second half of 2026. Other milestones (inaxaplin interim, povetacicept myasthenia gravis Phase 2) fall in H1 2027, with next earnings Feb 11.
- **Early FDA action:** Approval before Feb 28 is possible but unlikely soon. A complete response letter is the tail risk.

**Take for the journal**
- Five sessions into a three-month wait, the thesis is "delayed, not denied," with an unchanged business. A -7% gap on a flat close doesn't signal broken fundamentals.
- It is not a clean mean-reversion setup, though. The premium was event-driven. The stock is still near its 50-day average (525), and the catalysts that would fully restore it are months away. Dip-buying here is a bet that the 7% overshoots, not a catalyst trade.
- Risks to a long are the petition and any label surprise. A short is exposed to analyst support and rebounds in thin holiday trading.

- The net loss narrowed to RMB310M from RMB1.7B in Q2. Free cash flow was +RMB2.0B, and quarter-end cash was RMB88B.

  - Deliveries are guided to 110–115k, about 12–16% below the ~131k the market expected.
  - Revenue is guided to RMB31.7–33.1B, below the ~35.1B expected.
  - Management expects a return to profit in Q4.
- The stock rallied on margin and profit-turn evidence while the volume outlook disappointed.

   - October deliveries were only 29,025 (-8.6% year over year, the lowest since February).
   - November and December must average 40–43k a month to hit guidance.
   - Capacity for the new i6 was planned to reach 20k a month in November.
   - Dolphin Research cites third-party data showing weekly orders fading from about 54k in early November to about 17k in the second week.
